stem: A block of mass m is taken from A to B along a circular arc of radius R (centre O; A is vertically below O, B is horizontally to the right of O, angle AOB = 90°) under the action of a constant horizontal force F. Work done by this force is (a) FR (b) (π/2)FR (c) FR/√2 (d) FR/4

The small pendulum of mass m is suspended from a trolley that runs on a horizontal rail. The trolley and pendulum are initially at rest with θ = 0°. If the trolley is given a constant acceleration a, determine the maximum angle θ max through which the pendulum swings —

A ball of mass m is released from rest in a smooth circular tube of radius R (vertical plane), at the level of the centre. A spring of spring constant k, which is in its natural length, is placed in the tube as shown in figure (filling the arc from the ball down to the lowest point). If the angle made by the radius vector of the ball with the vertical when the ball comes to an instantaneous rest is 60°, then the value of k is (a) 9mg/(π²R) (b) 18mg/(π²R) (c) 36mg/(π²R) (d) 72mg/(π²R)

One end of a light spring of natural length d and spring constant k is fixed on a rigid wall and the other is fixed to a smooth ring of mass m which can slide without friction on a vertical rod fixed at a distance d from the wall. Initially the spring makes an angle 37° with the horizontal as shown in the figure. When the system is released from rest, find the speed of the ring when the spring becomes horizontal (sin 37° = 3/5) —

A small bob A of mass m is attached to a massless rigid rod of length 1 m pivoted at point P and kept at an angle of 60° with the vertical. At a distance of 1 m below point P, an identical bob B is kept at rest on a smooth horizontal surface that extends to a circular track of radius R. If bob B just manages to complete the circular path of radius R up to a point Q after being hit elastically by bob A, then radius R is ____ m — (a) 3/5 (b) 1/5 (c) (2+√3)/5 (d) (2−√3)/5 (JEE Main 2026, 23rd Jan Shift 1, Level-5) — (PYQ)

Two blocks with masses 100 g and 200 g are attached to the ends of springs A and B respectively, as shown in the figure (each spring hangs from the ceiling with its block at the bottom). The energy stored in A is E. The energy stored in B, when the spring constants k A , k B of A and B respectively satisfy the relation 4k A = 3k B , is — (a) 4E (b) 2E (c) 3E (d) (4/3)E (JEE Main 2026, 23rd Jan Shift 1, Level-3) — (PYQ)

A 5 kg block is simply released from the top of an inclined plane as shown in the figure: it slides 10 m down a frictionless (μ = 0) 30° incline, then travels 2 m along a rough horizontal stretch with μ = 0.5, and then hits a spring of constant k = 100 N/m (the surface under the spring is frictionless). The maximum compression in the spring when the block hits the spring is (g = 10 m/s²) (a) √6 m (b) √5 m (c) 1 m (d) 2 m

If the maximum load carried by an elevator is 1400 kg (600 kg – passengers + 800 kg – elevator), which is moving up with a uniform speed of 3 m s⁻¹, and the frictional force acting on it is 2000 N, then the maximum power used by the motor is ____ kW (g = 10 m s⁻²) (JEE Main 2023, Level-5) — (PYQ)
